indication_label: Paediatric and young adult (up to 25 y) B-cell ALL refractory, in relapse post-transplant or in second or later relapse
verbatim: Applying this estimate results in an annual eligible population for treatment with tisagenlecleucel of 400 patients.
source_doc: ICER, Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Therapy for B-Cell Cancers: Effectiveness and Value, Final Evidence Report, 23 March 2018
notes: Derivation (p.65-66): 2017 US ALL incidence 5,970 (SEER); under-25 cohort 3,651 (all under 20 plus 50% of 20-34); 82.5% B-ALL = 3,012; 3% refractory to initial therapy, 20% relapse; of relapsers 15% refractory to 2L and 36.5% relapse on 2L; result 400 per year.

indication_label: Paediatric and young adult r/r B-cell ALL (ICER executive summary budget-impact table)
verbatim: Table ES21. Estimated Annualized Total Potential Budget Impact (BI) of Tisagenlecleucel Using Different Prices Over a Five-year Time Horizon, Assuming 617 Eligible Patients per Year
source_doc: ICER, Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Therapy for B-Cell Cancers: Effectiveness and Value, Final Evidence Report, 23 March 2018
notes: Internal inconsistency in the ICER report: executive-summary Table ES21 title assumes 617 eligible per year while the body text derives 400 per year. Treat 400-617 as the ICER range.

indication_label: All ALL, US, all ages (denominator used by ICER)
unit: new cases per year (count, not rate)

source_doc: ICER, Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Therapy for B-Cell Cancers: Effectiveness and Value, Final Evidence Report, 23 March 2018
notes: Count not rate. ICER then takes 3,651 under age 25 and 82.5% B-lineage = 3,012 B-ALL under 25 per year: 'Of the 3,651 remaining ALL patients, we estimated that 82.5% would have B-ALL (3,012 patients).'

indication_label: ALL diagnosed at age 20 and younger, US; share who could benefit from Kymriah

source_doc: The Motley Fool, 'Novartis' $475,000 Price Tag Sets the Stage for a Price War With Gilead Sciences' (31 Aug 2017), reporting Novartis statements
notes: Arithmetic: 3,100 x 15% = 465; 3,100 x 20% = 620. The 3,100 and 15-20% are read in the secondary article (Novartis attribution); Novartis' own 30 Aug 2017 approval release (fetched) gives no patient count. A search summary also paraphrased 'about 600 would be considered candidates'.

notes: Upper bound only ('less than 100'). Page retrieved by curl (NICE returns 403 to the fetch tool). TA975 replaced TA554 (Dec 2018, CDF); TA554 resources page lists no resource impact document.

indication_label: Adult r/r DLBCL (incl. transplant-ineligible and post-ASCT relapse) after 2 or more lines of systemic therapy

source_doc: ICER, Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Therapy for B-Cell Cancers: Effectiveness and Value, Final Evidence Report, 23 March 2018
notes: Derivation p.66: DLBCL incidence 27,650 (2016, Teras et al.); 35% r/r = 9,678; 50% transplant-ineligible (4,839) of which 49% (2,371) failed salvage and eligible; transplant-eligible 4,839: 2,371 (49%) failed salvage plus 1,160 (47% of ASCT recipients not cured). ICER adds: 'we have not taken into consideration the current annual axicabtagene ciloleucel manufacturing capacity of 4,000 to 5,000 treatments per year.'

indication_label: DLBCL, US, all patients (denominator used by ICER)
unit: new cases per year (count, not rate)
verbatim: we first identified the incidence of DLBCL (27,650 patients in 2016) as reported in a 2016 observational study by Teras et al.
source_doc: ICER, Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Therapy for B-Cell Cancers: Effectiveness and Value, Final Evidence Report, 23 March 2018
notes: Count not rate. ICER: 'We assumed that 35% of all DLBCL patients relapsed or were refractory to chemotherapy' giving 9,678 r/r DLBCL per year.

indication_label: r/r DLBCL after first-line and salvage (US, all r/r DLBCL before fitness filters)
verbatim: Based on a review by Freidberg, 50% of the 9,678 relapsed/refractory DLBCL patients were transplant ineligible, of which 49% (2,371 patients) did not respond to salvage chemotherapy and were eligible for treatment with axicabtagene ciloleucel.
source_doc: ICER, Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Therapy for B-Cell Cancers: Effectiveness and Value, Final Evidence Report, 23 March 2018
notes: Intermediate ICER figure (35% of 27,650). Upper bound for any 2L+ CAR-T-eligible estimate in the US.

indication_label: 3L+ DLBCL patients in SEER-Medicare (aged 65+, fee-for-service Medicare), 2017-2020
unit: patients per year (Medicare SEER areas only)
verbatim: Between 2017 and 2020, 2241 patients were treated for 3L+ DLBCL in the SEER-Medicare data, of whom 122 (5.4%) received CAR-Ts.
source_doc: Blood Advances 2025, 'Inequalities in CAR T-cell therapy access for US patients with relapsed/refractory DLBCL: a SEER-Medicare data analysis' (PMC12466227)
notes: Arithmetic: 2,241 / 4 years = 560 per year, restricted to SEER-Medicare coverage (about a third of the US population, aged 65+). The fetch summary also paraphrased 'approximately 987 Medicare patients annually receive third-line or later therapy ... 6.3% of the roughly 15,673 total DLBCL cases'; those two numbers were not read verbatim and may belong to PMC12804711 (US claims study) instead.
excluded: SEER-Medicare areas only (about a third of the US population aged 65 and over); not a national eligible count

indication_label: Adult r/r DLBCL, US claims-based incidence and share reaching 3L
unit: new cases per year (count, not rate)

source_doc: Search-result snippet attributed to 'Real-world treatment patterns and clinical outcomes among patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma in a US healthcare claims database' (PMC12804711) or PMC12466227
notes: Snippet only; article not fetched. Implies 987 patients per year reach 3L on this base (4.68 per 100,000 x US population). A second snippet in the same search stated 'approximately 22,000 new diagnoses of DLBCL in the United States each year'.

indication_label: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and PMBCL after 2 or more systemic therapies (NICE TA872, routine commissioning)

notes: Page (retrieved by curl) only points to a combined Excel template covering TA872, TA927, TA947 and TA954; no eligible count is stated on the page. TA559 (Jan 2019, CDF) resources page lists no resource impact document either.

indication_label: LBCL needing second-line treatment, US (all 2L, before the refractory/early-relapse restriction)
source_doc: Derived from the Kite boilerplate above
notes: Arithmetic: 18,000 x 0.30 = 5,400; 18,000 x 0.40 = 7,200. Upper bound for the ZUMA-7 label population, which excludes relapses after 12 months and transplant-unfit patients.

notes: Same release: 'Although 60% of newly diagnosed LBCL patients, including those with DLBCL, will respond to their initial treatment, 40% will relapse or will not respond and need second-line treatment.' 'Up to' 38,000 is an upper bound.

indication_label: LBCL needing second-line treatment, Europe (all 2L)
source_doc: Derived from the Gilead 17 Oct 2022 release
notes: Arithmetic: 38,000 x 40% = 15,200 per year (upper bound; 'up to 38,000').

indication_label: Erwachsene mit DLBCL oder HGBL, das innerhalb von 12 Monaten nach Abschluss einer Erstlinien-Chemoimmuntherapie rezidiviert oder gegenüber dieser refraktär ist, und für die eine Hochdosistherapie infrage kommt

verbatim: This budget impact analysis included the estimated number of individuals ages 0 to 50 years with TDT in the US who would be eligible for treatment with beti-cel. Using this approach, we derived an estimate of 666 patients in the US eligible for treatment with beti-cel. Our estimate begins with prevalent cases of beta thalassemia in the US of roughly 2,100.48 From there, we assumed that about 63% of patients could be classified as having TDT arriving at approximately 1,333 patients.2 Of patients who are diagnosed with transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia, we assumed that 50% would be eligible for treatment with beti-cel, arriving at approximately 666 patients.

source_doc: SMC, eladocagene exuparvovec (Upstaza), Aug/Sep 2023, p.2
notes: 1 in 118,000 = 0.85 per 100,000 (my conversion). NHS Wales PP281 (Feb 2024) cites the same figure: 'The predicted birth rate is approximately 1 in 118,000 in the European Union'.

indication_label: known patients with AADC deficiency (all phenotypes)
verbatim: Clinical experts consulted by SMC advised that there are currently no known patients with AADC deficiency in Scotland; it is estimated that there are between 8 to 12 patients with AADC deficiency in the UK.
source_doc: SMC, eladocagene exuparvovec (Upstaza), Aug/Sep 2023, p.2
notes: Prevalent diagnosed pool, all ages/phenotypes; SMC notes about 80% of patients have the severe phenotype, so the label-eligible (severe, 18 months+) UK pool is roughly 6-10 (my arithmetic).

indication_label: estimated prevalence in the US based on CSF analysis and genetic testing
verbatim: AADC deficiency is an extremely rare disorder; there are less than 150 patients reported in the literature. AADC deficiency however, is probably underdiagnosed. The estimated prevalence in the U.S. based on cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis and genetic testing is roughly 1-3 in 100,000 live newborns. The predicted birth rate is approximately 1 in 118,000 in the European Union
source_doc: NHS Wales Joint Commissioning Committee, Specialised Services Policy Position Statement PP281, Eladocagene exuparvovec for treating AADC deficiency in people aged 18 months and over, Feb 2024, p.7
notes: Population base: live newborns.

indication_label: AADC deficiency incidence by region (literature digest)
verbatim: The incidence of AADC deficiency is estimated to range from 1 in 42,000-90,000 in the United States to 1 in 116,000 in Europe, and 1 in 162,000 in Japan.
source_doc: AADC Insights (aadcinsights.eu) publication digest, Prevalence of AADC deficiency, via WebSearch snippet
notes: Site fetch failed (TLS certificate mismatch); snippet only, underlying paper not identified. 1 in 90,000 = 1.1 and 1 in 42,000 = 2.4 per 100,000 (my conversion). Same digest: Japan 1 in 162,000 (0.62 per 100,000); Taiwan founder variant IVS6+4A>T predicted 1 in 32,000.

indication_label: AADC deficiency incidence (literature digest)
verbatim: 1 in 162,000 in Japan
source_doc: AADC Insights publication digest, via WebSearch snippet
notes: Snippet only. Japanese births not retrieved, so no derived count.

indication_label: AADC deficiency carrier frequency (gnomAD)
verbatim: The worldwide carrier frequency of AADC deficiency was 0.17%; the highest frequency was observed in East Asians at 0.78%, and the lowest was in Latinos at 0.07%.
source_doc: Carrier frequency and incidence of aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase deficiency: a gnomAD-based study. Pediatric Research 2023 (PubMed 37286773), via WebSearch snippet
notes: Nature.com redirected to an auth page and PubMed showed only a cookie wall; snippet only. Incidence figures from this paper were not captured.

indication_label: babies born with AADC deficiency per year (all phenotypes)
source_doc: Derived from CDC 2023 births and incidence range
notes: Derived: 3,591,328 / 118,000 (EU predicted rate, SMC) = 30; x 1-3 per 100,000 (NHS Wales, US estimate) = 36-108; / 40,000 (PTC upper bound) = 90. US label has no severity restriction; roughly 80% severe (SMC) if a severe-only pool is wanted (24-86).

indication_label: babies born with AADC deficiency per year, and severe-phenotype flow
source_doc: Derived from Eurostat 2024 births, SMC/PTC incidence and SMC severe share
notes: Derived: 3,550,000 / 118,000 = 30 to / 40,000 = 89 born per year; x 80% severe phenotype (SMC) = 24-71 label-eligible flow (18 months+ so entry lags birth by 1.5 years).

indication_label: babies born with AADC deficiency per year, and severe-phenotype flow
source_doc: Derived from ONS 2023 births, SMC/PTC incidence and SMC severe share
notes: Derived: 563,561 / 118,000 = 4.8 to / 40,000 = 14 born per year; x 80% severe = 4-11. Compare SMC's prevalent UK pool of 8-12 diagnosed patients (all ages), which implies most incident cases are undiagnosed or the true incidence is at the low end.

indication_label: biallelic RPE65-mediated inherited retinal disease (ICER candidate population, no viable-cell restriction)
verbatim: The US population represents approximately 50.06% of the total population in the US and the five major European markets (Germany, France, Italy, Spain and the United Kingdom). Applying that proportion to the total of 3,500 patients results in an estimate of approximately 1,750 eligible individuals in the US.
source_doc: ICER, Voretigene Neparvovec for Biallelic RPE65-Mediated Retinal Disease: Effectiveness and Value, Final Evidence Report, 14 Feb 2018, section 4.3 Potential Budget Impact
notes: ICER budget-impact candidate population = all US individuals with biallelic RPE65 IRD, derived from Spark's 10-K figure of 3,500 in US+EU5; no adjustment for 'sufficient viable retinal cells'. Text extracted from the PDF locally.

indication_label: biallelic RPE65-mediated IRD (ICER five-year spread of the prevalent pool)

notes: Budget-impact convention (1,750 / 5), not an incidence estimate. ICER: 'the relatively small number of patients assumed to be treated per year (350)'. Actual US treated numbers (75 vials in 2018) were far below this.
excluded: ICER budget-impact assumption spreading the prevalent pool over five years; not an incident inflow

indication_label: persons in the US with RPE65-mediated IRDs (manufacturer preliminary estimate as cited by ICER)

source_doc: ICER, Voretigene Neparvovec for Biallelic RPE65-Mediated Retinal Disease: Effectiveness and Value, Final Evidence Report, 14 Feb 2018, section 1 Background
notes: ICER citing Spark (its reference 9). Wider than Spark's own 1,000-2,000 (3 Jan 2018 release, already in luxturna_disclosures.csv). Not restricted to viable retinal cells.

indication_label: individuals with RPE65-mediated inherited retinal diseases
geography: US and EU5 (Germany, France, Italy, Spain, UK)
verbatim: we used inputs from a US Securities and Exchange Commission Form 10-K Annual Report by Spark Therapeutics, Inc., which estimated "that there are approximately 3,500 individuals with RPE65-mediated inherited retinal diseases in the United States and the five major European markets."
source_doc: ICER, Voretigene Neparvovec for Biallelic RPE65-Mediated Retinal Disease: Effectiveness and Value, Final Evidence Report, 14 Feb 2018, section 4.3, quoting Spark Therapeutics Form 10-K

indication_label: LCA or RP with biallelic RPE65 mutations, GKV-insured (before viable-cell restriction)
verbatim: Die Zahlen basieren auf Praevalenzdaten von Patienten mit Leberscher kongenitaler Amaurose (LCA) und Retinitis pigmentosa (RP), jeweils mit biallelischen RPE65-Mutationen; es ergibt sich unter Beruecksichtigung der niedrigsten und hoechsten Praevalenz eine Spanne aus dem minimalen und maximalen Anteil von 188 bis 655 Patienten (im Mittel 355 Patienten).
source_doc: G-BA, Tragende Gruende zum Beschluss ueber die Nutzenbewertung von Voretigen Neparvovec (Luxturna), 17 Oct 2019, section 2.2
notes: Manufacturer (Novartis) dossier figures adopted by G-BA; mean 355. GKV covers about 88% of the German population. Umlauts transliterated in verbatim.

indication_label: label population incl. 'ausreichend lebensfaehige Netzhautzellen', GKV-insured
verbatim: In einem naechsten Schritt findet der minimale und maximale Anteil behandelbarer Patienten Beruecksichtigung; die resultierende Patientenpopulation von ca. 100 bis 530 Patienten ergibt sich aus dem zugelassenen Anwendungsgebiet, das auf diejenigen Patienten mit "ausreichend lebensfaehigen Netzhautzellen" einschraenkt. Die Berechnung des Umfangs der Zielpopulation liegt in der Gesamtschau in einer plausiblen Groessenordnung, ist jedoch mit Unsicherheiten behaftet.
source_doc: G-BA, Tragende Gruende zum Beschluss ueber die Nutzenbewertung von Voretigen Neparvovec (Luxturna), 17 Oct 2019, section 2.2
notes: Official G-BA eligible count for Germany (statutory insurance). Prevalent pool at EU launch; G-BA calls the order of magnitude plausible but uncertain. | family set by override: G-BA target population for a one-time therapy is the prevalent pool at launch (duplicate of the prevalent row)

[...] die resultierende Patientenpopulation von ca. 100 bis 530 Patientinnen und Patienten ergibt sich aus dem zugelassenen Anwendungsgebiet, das auf diejenigen Patientinnen und Patienten mit "ausreichend lebensfaehigen Netzhautzellen" einschraenkt.
source_doc: G-BA, Tragende Gruende zum Beschluss (Neubewertung nach Fristablauf) Voretigen Neparvovec, 15 Sep 2022, section 2.2

indication_label: adults with idiopathic macular telangiectasia type 2 (US label)
verbatim: ENCELTO is an allogeneic encapsulated cell-based gene therapy indicated for the treatment of adults with idiopathic macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel).
source_doc: Neurotech Pharmaceuticals press release with Highlights of Prescribing Information, 'Neurotech's ENCELTO Approved by the FDA for the Treatment of Macular Telangiectasia Type 2', 6 Mar 2025
notes: Adults only; one implant per affected eye (disease is usually bilateral), so implants per patient can approach 2. The press release gives no prevalence or patient-number statement. US availability from June 2025. Not approved outside the US as of Sep 2026.

indication_label: MacTel type 2 detected on fundus photographs, adults aged 43-86
verbatim: a prevalence of 0.1% in the age group analyzed
source_doc: Charbel Issa P et al., Macular telangiectasia type 2, Prog Retin Eye Res 2013 (PMC3638089), section on prevalence, citing Klein R et al., The prevalence of macular telangiectasia type 2 in the Beaver Dam Eye Study, Am J Ophthalmol 2010
notes: Population base: 4,790 Beaver Dam Eye Study participants aged 43-86 at baseline (1988-90), regraded from stereoscopic fundus photographs; PubMed abstract (20609708, cookie-walled) gives 95% CI 0.09-0.1. Highest published estimate; the review says photo-based grading likely underestimates true prevalence.

indication_label: MacTel type 2 on non-mydriatic macular images, mean age 65
verbatim: a lower prevalence, estimated to range from 0.004 to 0.022%
source_doc: Charbel Issa P et al., Macular telangiectasia type 2, Prog Retin Eye Res 2013 (PMC3638089), section on prevalence, citing Aung KZ et al., Melbourne Collaborative Cohort Study, 2010
notes: Just over 22,000 participants; images were graded for MacTel only if an earlier grading flagged a feature, so probably an undercount. Kenya/Nigeria population studies (Sallo 2012) gave 0.06% (combined 95% CI 0.02-0.14%).

indication_label: MacTel type 2, all adults (0.1% prevalence applied to the US population)
verbatim: MacTel type 2 impacts around 0.1% of the population, translating to approximately 165,000 patients in the United States.
source_doc: Claritas Rx blog, 'A Breakthrough in Vision Care: The FDA Approval of Neurotech's Encelto', 2025 (citing Endpoints News, endpts.com/fda-approves-neurotech-therapy-for-rare-eye-disease/)
notes: Trade-press arithmetic, not a Neurotech statement; blog undated (approval date used). 0.1% of the whole US population would be about 335,000, so 165,000 implies 0.1% applied to roughly the population over 40. Upper-bound prevalent pool; most are undiagnosed and many have late disease beyond the trial population.

indication_label: MacTel type 2, US population aged 45 and over, published prevalence range
source_doc: Derived here from Beaver Dam (0.1%) and Melbourne (0.004%) rates x US population aged 45+ (about 139 million: 2020 Census, ages 45-64 plus 65+)
notes: 0.004% x 139m = 5,560; 0.1% x 139m = 139,000. Neither rate is diagnosis-based; the diagnosed, adult, idiopathic pool eligible under the label is far smaller and undocumented.

indication_label: severe-to-profound/profound SNHL with biallelic OTOF variants, preserved outer hair cell function, no prior cochlear implant in the same ear (US label)
verbatim: For the treatment of pediatric and adult patients with severe-to-profound and profound sensorineural hearing loss (HL; any frequency >90 dB) associated with molecularly confirmed biallelic variants in the OTOF gene, preserved outer hair cell function, and no prior cochlear implant in the same ear.
source_doc: FDA, OTARMENI (lunsotogene parvec-cwha) product page, STN 125874, Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, approval 23 Apr 2026
notes: Accelerated approval. The no-prior-implant and preserved-OHC criteria exclude most prevalent OTOF-deaf people (already implanted or with degraded OHC function), so the eligible pool is essentially the annual flow of newly diagnosed infants plus a small backlog of unimplanted ears. Regeneron provides the product free in the US, so treated patients will not appear in revenue. No ex-US approval.

indication_label: newborns per year with OTOF-related hearing loss

source_doc: CGTLive, 'Regeneron Nets Accelerated Approval From FDA for Otoferlin-Related Hearing Loss Gene Therapy Lunsotogene Parvec', 24 Apr 2026 (reporting Regeneron's figure)
notes: Secondary report of the company estimate; Regeneron's own release (investor.regeneron.com and newsroom mirror) timed out on three attempts. CHORD pivotal cohort: 20 participants aged 10 months to 16 years.

source_doc: Ultragenyx press release, 'Ultragenyx Announces U.S. FDA Approval of GENGLYCOS Gene Therapy...', 19 Aug 2026 (GlobeNewswire)

indication_label: glycogen storage disease type I (Ia = 80%)

source_doc: Nana M, Anastasopoulou C, Parikh NS, Ahlawat R, Glycogen Storage Disease Type I, StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf NBK534196), last update 6 Apr 2025

indication_label: GSDIa births per year (become label-eligible at age 8)
source_doc: Derived here: 3.6 million US live births per year (CDC 2023: about 3.59m) x 1/100,000 x 0.8 (GSDIa share, StatPearls)
notes: 3,600,000 / 100,000 x 0.8 = 28.8. The annual flow into label eligibility is the birth cohort reaching age 8 (about 30/yr), assuming full survival. Company prevalent estimate (1,500-2,500) implies a mean prevalence of roughly 0.5-0.75 per 100,000, consistent with this incidence.

indication_label: adults with genetically confirmed familial LPLD, severe or multiple pancreatitis attacks despite low-fat diet, detectable LPL protein (EU label)

indication_label: wound treatment from birth in DEB with mutation(s) in COL7A1 (EU label)
verbatim: Demnach ist Beremagen geperpavec zur Wundbehandlung bei Patientinnen und Patienten ab der Geburt mit dystropher Epidermolysis bullosa (DEB) mit Mutation(en) im Gen fuer die Alpha-1-Kette von Kollagen Typ VII (COL7A1) zugelassen [1].

indication_label: Relapsed or refractory CLL/SLL after at least two prior lines including a BTK inhibitor and a BCL-2 inhibitor (US accelerated approval, March 2024)
verbatim: The FDA granted accelerated approval of Breyanzi for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma who have received at least two prior lines of therapy, including a Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor and a B-cell lymphoma 2 inhibitor.
source_doc: BMS 8-K Ex-99.1 Q1-2024 earnings release (25 Apr 2024); BMS ASCO 2024 Breyanzi release boilerplate (news.bms.com); BusinessWire approval release (403); Europe PMC search for US double-exposed CLL population estimates
notes: No BMS statement of a US eligible count was found; BMS boilerplate gives no CLL incidence. ICER has not reviewed Breyanzi in CLL. No G-BA procedure exists for liso-cel in CLL (G-BA lists only LBCL 3L D-867, LBCL 2L D-951 and FL 3L D-1196), so no German count either. Europe PMC query for US real-world double-exposed/double-refractory CLL population estimates returned nothing usable. Existing E1a denominator: ~22,760 new CLL cases per year (ACS).

indication_label: Relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma after two or more lines of systemic therapy (US accelerated approval, May 2024)
verbatim: FL is the second most common form of NHL and the most common subtype of indolent NHL, accounting for 20 to 30 percent of all NHL cases.
source_doc: BMS Breyanzi ASCO 2024 press release boilerplate (news.bms.com, 2024); BMS Q1-2024 8-K; Europe PMC
notes: No US 3L+ FL flow found from BMS, ICER or NICE (NICE has no liso-cel FL appraisal; TA1159 covers 3L LBCL). Germany figure of 370-840 GKV patients per year (this file) can be scaled: Germany GKV ~74m insured vs US ~340m population implies roughly 1,700-3,900 per year in the US if treatment patterns were identical (not recorded as a value; population-scaling across systems is unreliable).

indication_label: Relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma after at least two prior lines including a BTK inhibitor (US accelerated approval, May 2024)
verbatim: MCL is an aggressive, rare form of NHL, representing roughly 3% of all NHL cases.
source_doc: BMS Breyanzi ASCO 2024 press release boilerplate; BMS Q1-2024 8-K; Europe PMC search for US post-BTKi MCL treatment-pattern studies
notes: No US count located. Europe PMC returned only a BTKi adherence study (402 community-oncology MCL patients initiating a BTKi 2019-2021), not a national flow. indication_label: Adultos con mieloma múltiple en recaída y refractario tras al menos una línea previa (IMiD y IP), progresión al último tratamiento y refractarios a lenalidomida
verbatim: La Comisión Interministerial de Precios de los Medicamentos, en su sesión de 26 de febrero de 2025, acordó proponer a la Dirección General de Cartera Común del SNS y Farmacia la inclusión en la prestación farmacéutica del SNS de este medicamento y su financiación para el tratamiento de pacientes adultos con mieloma múltiple en recaída y refractario que han recibido al menos una línea previa de tratamiento, incluidos un agente inmunomodulador y un inhibidor del proteasoma, han presentado progresión de la enfermedad al último tratamiento y son refractarios a lenalidomida.
source_doc: Ministerio de Sanidad, Informe público sobre la decisión de inclusión en la prestación farmacéutica de ciltacabtagén autoleucel (Carvykti) (26 May 2025); AEMPS IPT-339/V1/29012025 Carvykti (full text grepped)
notes: Neither the CIPM public report nor IPT-339 states an eligible or expected patient number; financing is under a pay-for-results agreement (PFS-based) within the Plan de Abordaje de las Terapias Avanzadas, with a protocolo farmacoclínico dated 1 Apr 2025 (https://www.sanidad.gob.es/areas/farmacia/infoMedicamentos/terapiasAvanzadas/docs/01042025_Protocolo_farmacoclinico_ciltacabtagen_autoleucel_mmrr_2l.pdf, not fetched). IPT-339 gives Spanish MM incidence 5.3-6.9 per 100,000 per year (2020) and 16,307 prevalent cases in 2020 (8,925 men, 7,382 women).

indication_label: LBCL refractory to or relapsed within 12 months of first-line therapy and intended for autologous SCT (2L axi-cel eligible), US budget-impact model
unit: patients per 1,000,000 health-plan members per year
verbatim: It was estimated that 9 patients in a million member plan would be eligible for axi-cel treatment as 2L LBCL patients.
source_doc: Perales MA, Kuruvilla J, Snider JT, Vadgama S, Blissett R, El-Moustaid F, Smith NJ, Patel AR, Johnston PB. The Cost-Effectiveness of Axicabtagene Ciloleucel as Second-Line Therapy in Patients with Large B-Cell Lymphoma in the United States: An Economic Evaluation of the ZUMA-7 Trial. Transplant Cell Ther 2022;28(11):750.e1-750.e6 (doi 10.1016/j.jtct.2022.08.010)
notes: Kite-funded economic evaluation, but the method is published: BIM inputs table gives incidence of LBCL 54 per 1,000,000 (SEER), primary refractory disease 15% and relapsed disease 25% (Sehn 2021), proportion relapsed within 12 months 70% (Maurer 2014), proportion intended for auto-SCT 50% (Friedberg 2011); 54 x (0.15 + 0.25 x 0.70) x 0.50 = 8.8 per million. This is the independent (methods-stated) counterpart to the Kite boilerplate 5,400-7,200 in E1a.
excluded: a rate (9 eligible per million plan members, Perales 2022), not a count; the derived national flow from the same source is kept

indication_label: LBCL refractory to or relapsed within 12 months of first-line therapy, all-comers (US label population, no transplant-intent filter)
verbatim: Incidence of LBCL 54/1,000,000 ... SEER; Primary refractory disease 15% ... Sehn 2021; Relapsed disease 25% ... Sehn 2021; Proportion relapsed within 12 months 70% Maurer 2014; Proportion intended for auto-SCT 50% ... Friedberg 2011
source_doc: Derived from the Perales 2022 BIM inputs (SEER, Sehn 2021, Maurer 2014) and the US Census Bureau Vintage 2024 resident population
notes: Arithmetic: 54 per million x 340,110,988 US residents (1 July 2024) = 18,366 LBCL cases per year; early relapse/refractory share = 15% + 25% x 70% = 32.5%; 18,366 x 0.325 = 5,969 per year. The US label (Yescarta Apr 2022, Breyanzi Jun 2022) does not require transplant intent (Breyanzi also covers transplant-ineligible patients), so this is the label flow; the transplant-intended subset is 5,969 x 50% = 2,984 (or 9 per million x 340.1m = 3,061 using the paper rounding). Sits at the low end of the Kite boilerplate 5,400-7,200 range in E1a.

indication_label: LBCL refractory to or relapsed within 12 months of first-line therapy, US (same population as the Yescarta 2L label plus transplant-ineligible patients)
